abstract: Teratocarcinoma is a mixed germ cell tumor histologically composed of embryonal carcinoma cells and embryonic and extraembryonic tissues. In the present work we have used the CE44 teratocarcinoma, which is a tumor cell line derived from the OTT6050 experimental tumor, to appreciate the influence the microenvironment has on the modulation of tumoral differentiation. For this, we have studied the development of CE44 teratocarcinoma in primary tumors (subcutaneous and intrasplenic) and in experimental metastases (hepatic and pulmonary). CE44 teratocarcinoma shows variations in its capacity for differentiation in so far as development is concerned and, in hepatic metastases, we noticed a reparative process of the intratumoral necrotic areas which in the same cases were substituted by loose connective tissue. Our results clearly suggest that the microenvironment is decisive in the biological behaviour of the teratocarcinoma cells and that epigenetic factors influence the capacity for differentiation of the undifferentiated tumoral cells.
abstract_ja: 奇形癌は、胎児性癌細胞と胚性および胚外組織から構成される混合型胚細胞腫瘍である。本研究では、実験的腫瘍OTT6050に由来する腫瘍細胞株CE44奇形癌を用い、微小環境が腫瘍の分化に及ぼす修飾を検討した。このため、原発腫瘍(皮下および脾内)および実験的転移(肝および肺)におけるCE44奇形癌の発育を検討した。CE44奇形癌は、発育に関して分化能に変化を示した。また、肝転移では腫瘍内の壊死領域の修復過程がみられ、同一症例では壊死領域が疎な結合組織に置換されていた。本研究の結果は、微小環境が奇形癌細胞の生物学的挙動において決定的であり、エピジェネティックな要因が未分化腫瘍細胞の分化能に影響を及ぼすことを明確に示唆している。
